caption: The drawing depicts a lidded vessel, likely a sugar bowl, rendered in pencil on a light tan background. The central object is a symmetrical, rounded container with a fitted domed lid that features a finial on top. The body of the vessel has two angular handles, one on each side, extending upward from the sides and curving slightly outward. Around the top section of the bowl just below the lid, there is a decorative band with a repeating interlocking oval or geometric pattern. The center of the main body has an ornate oval cartouche, adorned with scrollwork and flourishes, containing an elaborate monogram. Below the main image, the name "Hester Duany" is written in small script. In the lower left and right corners, there are two smaller sketched diagrams of the vessel: the left one shows a side view, and the right one presents a front view with measurements. The overall drawing is monochromatic, utilizing differing intensities of pencil shading to illustrate the metallic texture and three-dimensional form of the vessel.
title: Silver Sugar Bowl with Cover
